questions.q: What distinguishes linear emission from decaying emission?
options: Linear emission never has a reserve limit; decaying always does
They are two names for the same mechanism
Linear emission only applies to NFTs
Linear pays a constant rate per block until the reserve runs out; decaying shrinks the rate on a schedule, often by halving
questions.explain: Linear emission releases a constant number of tokens per block/epoch; decaying emission reduces the rate over time, commonly via periodic halving.

questions.q: At 10 tokens/block and 2,000,000 blocks/year, how long does a 100,000,000-token reserve last under linear emission?
options: 1 year
5 years
10 years
50 years

questions.q: Why can a decaying (halving-style) emission schedule create more "farm and dump" behavior than a linear one?
options: Decaying schedules always pay out more tokens in total
It has no effect on farmer behavior compared to linear emission
It explicitly signals that the rate will decline, pushing early farmers to maximize the current rate and sell immediately before it drops
Decaying schedules eliminate sell pressure entirely
questions.explain: A decaying schedule tells participants emissions are richest now, which incentivizes farming hard and selling fast before the next halving reduces the rate.

questions.q: What are the three moves this lesson describes for tapering an emission schedule toward sustainability?
options: Bootstrap high, taper on a defined/announced schedule, shift the weight toward real fee-based yield
Pay emissions forever at a fixed rate with no changes
Stop all emissions immediately at launch
Only increase emissions over time, never decrease
questions.explain: The lesson describes bootstrapping with high emissions, tapering on a predictable schedule, and shifting the reward mix toward real yield as fee revenue grows.

questions.q: Under the halving example (initial rate 50 tokens/block, halving every 210,000 blocks), what is the reward rate for blocks 210,001-420,000?
options: 50 tokens/block
12.5 tokens/block
0 tokens/block
25 tokens/block
questions.explain: After the first halving interval, the rate drops to half of 50, which is 25 tokens/block.
